skill.name: scanpy
skill.description: Provides Scanpy guidance for single-cell RNA-seq workflows, including data loading, QC, normalization, dimensionality reduction, clustering, marker genes, annotation, trajectory analysis, and reporting.
skill.summary: Guide Scanpy workflows for reproducible single-cell RNA-seq analysis.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Single-cell RNA-seq workflows require careful QC, normalization, clustering, and documentation. This skill gives Scanpy workflows, scripts, templates, and references for reproducible analysis.
actual_capabilities: Guides Scanpy loading for .h5ad, 10X HDF5, 10X MTX, and CSV data.
Provides QC metrics, filtering thresholds, and before-and-after plot workflow.
Covers normalization, log transform, highly variable genes, scaling, PCA, UMAP, and t-SNE.
Shows Leiden clustering, marker gene ranking, manual annotation, and differential expression.
Includes a reusable analysis template and QC script for local datasets.
limitations: Requires a working Python environment with Scanpy and related packages installed.
Does not download datasets or call remote analysis services.
Cell type labels require domain expertise and marker validation.
Large datasets may require memory tuning outside the template.

use_cases.title: Run Initial Dataset QC
use_cases.description: Run quality control and clustering on a new 10X or h5ad dataset.

use_cases.title: Build Reproducible Workflows
use_cases.description: Create a Scanpy workflow with saved outputs and documented parameters.

use_cases.title: Prepare Analysis Figures
use_cases.description: Compare markers, trajectories, and condition effects before preparing figures.

prompt_templates.title: Run Initial QC
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Scanpy skill to plan QC for my h5ad file. Include metrics, thresholds, plots, and expected outputs.

prompt_templates.title: Build Standard Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Scanpy workflow for loading 10X data, normalizing cells, clustering, and saving results. Explain each analysis choice.

prompt_templates.title: Tune Clustering Choices
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Scanpy results and suggest clustering resolutions, PCA dimensions, and neighbor settings to test next. Include validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Publication Analysis
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an advanced Scanpy analysis plan with marker ranking, annotation validation, differential expression, trajectory checks, and publication figures.

output_examples.input: User asks for QC on a PBMC h5ad file.
output_examples.output: The response lists QC metrics, plot names, threshold ranges, filtering steps, and saved filtered data outputs.

output_examples.input: User asks how to annotate clusters.
output_examples.output: The response recommends marker genes, dot plots, UMAP checks, a cluster-to-cell-type table, and validation notes.
The response proposes UMAP, heatmap, dot plot, violin plot, and export settings for figure-ready files.

best_practices: Save raw counts before filtering genes.
Adjust QC thresholds from dataset-specific plots.
Validate annotations with multiple marker genes.
anti_patterns: Do not reuse thresholds without checking data quality.
Do not treat cluster numbers as biological labels.
Do not skip intermediate outputs for long workflows.

faq.question: What data formats does it support?
faq.answer: The examples cover h5ad, 10X HDF5, 10X MTX directories, and CSV files.

faq.question: Can it run QC automatically?
faq.answer: Yes. The bundled QC script loads local data, makes plots, filters cells and genes, and writes a filtered h5ad file.

faq.question: Does it install Scanpy?
faq.answer: No. You must provide a Python environment with Scanpy and its dependencies.

faq.question: Can it annotate cell types?
faq.answer: It supports manual annotation using marker genes. Final labels should be validated by a domain expert.

faq.question: Does it use network services?
faq.answer: No analysis step calls remote services. The documentation links to public Scanpy resources.

faq.question: Can it handle large datasets?
faq.answer: Yes, but memory and runtime depend on the local machine and dataset size.
